<Rep. Robert Garcia>: H.R. 8464, the Stopping Fraudulent Payments Act, would add a new section to title 31 U.S.C. giving the Treasury the authority to pause and segment payments. It would require agencies to take corrective action prior to certifying a payment voucher request if there is an identified risk of fraud or an improper payment that would result in a financial loss to the government. It would require the Treasury to return such payment requests to the agency for corrective action.
Committee Democrats strongly oppose H.R. 8464. In the face of a deepening cost of living crisis, with growing economic anxiety across the nation, the American people rely on critical federal programs to make ends meet. This bill could make that harder for some Americans due to process delays. This bill aims to stop improper payments, which we all agree is important. Unfortunately, it uses vague criteria which will stop many legitimate payments, causing more red tape, delays, and dysfunction.
The current Administration has a long record of wrongly delaying payments for political reasons. Just last month, citing unsubstantiated concerns about fraud in hospice care, it suspended $1.3 billion in Medicaid payments to California. That could harm nearly a million elderly and disabled residents of the state. Last December, it threatened to withhold SNAP benefits from Colorado and Minnesota. In January, the Department of Health and Human Services froze $10 billion for essential needs in funding to five states led by Democratic governors.
It is against this backdrop that we must consider H.R. 8464. This bill would allow agencies to delay payments if they have ``sufficient reason'' that the payment has an ``elevated risk of fraud.'' This creates a significant amount of discretion for agency officials. This discretion could be misused for partisan political purposes.
The bill's stated intent is to stop improper payments, which we all agree is important. However, millions of Americans rely on critical federal programs for health care, food, and rent to make ends meet.
The American people want programs to work, not unnecessary red tape, delayed legitimate payments, and dysfunction.
Robert Garcia,
Ranking Member.
